subject: Post-call: Model fit & evals follow-up \u0007 tool-calling / structured output
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps - Model fit & evals (tool-calling / structured output)

Hi Jane / Alex -

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you a targeted eval: 

What we heard:
- Use case: DeltaWorks wants an in-product assistant that can surface account-level recommendations and kick off internal workflows (ticket create, send SLA notice).
- Data access: read-only access to DeltaWorks CRM + ability to post back via authenticated webhook for actions.
- Constraints: JSON-structured responses required for downstream automation (strict schema), retries on webhook failures, and latency target ~350ms P50 for single-turn lookups.

Proposed Redwood scope for the eval:
1) Model fit comparison across three model families (smaller low-latency quantized vs medium-sized for quality vs high-quality tuned variant).
2) Eval set: we'll run your prompt set (sample attached) + 200 synthetic prompts we generate to stress schema edge cases.
3) Tool-calling tests: structured JSON compliance, varying failure modes (timeout, 5xx, invalid schema).
4) Metrics: schema pass-rate, exact-key match rate, average token cost, P50/P95 latency, successful retry rate after transient failures.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Deliver a short benchmark report with recommended model/config and example prompt engineering notes (ETA 7 business days after we get access to the sample prompt set and a small dataset).
- Two short demo sessions: (1) results walkthrough, (2) integration test against your staging webhook.

Action items:
- Jane: share the sample prompt set + a staging webhook URL (or allow test harness to call a mock endpoint).
- Marissa/Rishi: provide evaluation plan and preliminary model recommendations.
- Aditya: will set up a sandbox project and share credentials for the limited eval run.

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.json (sample prompts), redwood_benchmarks.pdf (overview)

Thanks - I'll coordinate internally and aim to get the eval plan over by Tue EOD.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - this looks great. A couple clarifications: 

1) Prompt set: I attached an expanded set (see prompt-set-v1.json you already received) - we'll add 50 more real examples by EOD tomorrow.
2) Webhook: staging webhook is https://staging.deltaworks.com/hooks/redwood-test (auth token I'll share in a separate secure note).
3) Failure modes: we care about idempotency on retries (don't create duplicate tickets) and explicit error codes in the JSON when the assistant cannot fulfill an action.

One ask: can you include a quick check for JSON schema strictness that also tolerates minor ordering differences but enforces required fields and types? That's our biggest integration risk.

We're excited to see the results - happy to be available for a quick 30m sync if you want to walk through the prompt set.

- Jane

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - Model fit & evals (tool-calling / structured output)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Jane. High level responses to your asks and our planned approach: 

JSON schema checks
- We'll implement a two-tier validation: (A) strict required fields and type checks (fail), (B) lenient ordering/extra-fields tolerance (warn). The eval will report pass/fail and list examples where additional key normalization was necessary.

Model recommendations (initial)
- Fast low-cost option: small quantized family (q2_klein) - good for lookups and short structured outputs, P50 ~180-240ms in our hosted benchmarks but lower generation quality on ambiguous prompts.
- Balanced: mid-family (redwood-2.7b-std) - better instruction-following and structured output fidelity, P50 ~280-350ms depending on batch size and kv-cache hits.
- High-quality: tuned variant (redwood-7b-tuned) - highest schema adherence on complex transforms but higher token cost and latency P50 ~420-550ms.

Tool-calling retries
- We'll simulate transient failures and verify client-side retries (exponential backoff) plus a server-side idempotency key field to dedupe ticket creation.

Next steps
1) Rishi/Aditya - can you confirm the eval harness will generate the schema edge-case set and instrument webhook retry scenarios?
2) Jane - once you drop the extra 50 examples and secure token, we'll start the run.

I'll attach an internal eval plan shortly.

Best,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps - Model fit & evals (tool-calling / structured output)

Looping in implementation details and the eval checklist we'll use. Summary below - full plan in shared drive (link in metadata).

Eval checklist (implementation notes):
- Data ingestion: use provided prompt-set-v1.json + 50 real examples from DeltaWorks to create combined eval corpus (~300 examples).
- Schema tests: use JSON Schema draft-07 for validation. We'll run three validators: strict (exact types & required), normalized (cast numeric strings when safe), and permissive (warn-only). Report will include pass-rate per validator.
- Model config matrix: { models: ["q2_klein", "redwood-2.7b-std", "redwood-7b-tuned"], temps: [0.0, 0.2, 0.4], max_tokens: [150, 400] }
- Tool-calling tests: 3 simulated failure modes: webhook timeout (>=5s), webhook 500, webhook 429. For each failure we test 3 retry policies (0/2/5 retries) with idempotency key and check duplicate actions.
- Metrics captured: schema_pass_rate_strict, schema_pass_rate_normalized, avg_cost_per_call_usd, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, successful_retry_rate, duplicates_detected_count.

Action: Aditya will provision a sandbox project and share creds by EOD. I'll kick off the harness once creds + token are in.

Notes on structured output generation: please pay attention to trailing commas and number-vs-string ambiguity for IDs - these are our most common failure modes when downstream systems strictly type-check. We'll include targeted prompts to force numeric/string variants.

- Rishi
Principal Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

Happy to schedule the quick demo after the first run completes. Looking forward to the report.
